title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for residual stroke symptoms.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, BMI 28.4.

Recent Labs: HbA1c 6.8%, eGFR 88 mL/min/1.73m2, Lipid Panel: Total Cholesterol 190 mg/dL, LDL 102 mg/dL, HDL 45 mg/dL, Triglycerides 150 mg/dL.

History of Present Illness:
[Copied Forward from 03/15/2026]
Patient is a 51-year-old male presenting for follow-up regarding a past ischemic stroke. He reports stable baseline symptoms but notes ongoing right-sided hemiparesis. He is left-hand dominant and manages most activities of daily living independently despite the physical limitations. He denies any recent falls or worsening of motor function.

[Update]
The patient reports that his right-sided hemiparesis remains stable. He is able to perform most tasks using his left hand. He denies any new balance issues or changes in sensation. He continues to participate in a regular stretching routine.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily
- Aspirin 81mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
Neurological: Positive for right-sided hemiparesis. Negative for dizziness or loss of consciousness.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for decreased strength in right upper and lower extremities.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for abdominal pain or changes in bowel habits.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria or incontinence.

Social History:
The patient is married and works as a software engineer. He lives in a single-story home. He exercises three times a week and does not smoke.

Family History:
Father had a myocardial infarction at age 62. Mother has hypertension.

Exam:
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
Neurological: Grossly intact sensation to light touch in all extremities. Significant right-sided hemiparesis noted in the right arm and leg. Strength is 3/5 in the right upper extremity and 4/5 in the right lower extremity. Reflexes are 2+ throughout. Cranial nerves II-XII are grossly intact. Gait is steady with a slight limp on the right side.

Assessment:
1. Residual right-sided hemiparesis following a prior ischemic stroke.
2. Hyperlipidemia.

Plan:
1. Continue current medications.
2. Encourage continued physical therapy for right-sided hemiparesis.
3. Routine follow-up in 3 months.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 10/14/2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, right non-dominant side: I69.353 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
